title: Tag Directory Size: What One Line Really Costs
unit: Memory Interfacing, Hierarchy and Cache Mapping
quickIdea: The directory costs (tag + valid + dirty + replacement bits) x number of lines, and GATE asks for it with the tag width left for you to derive.
remember: Entries = number of lines = cache data size / block size. There is one entry per line, not per set.
Bits per entry = tag width + 1 valid bit + (1 dirty bit if write-back) + any replacement bits the question names.
Total directory = entries x bits per entry. Give it in bits or in Kbits as asked; the options usually differ by a factor of 8 or by one bit per entry.
The tag width comes from the address split: address width - log2(lines) - log2(block size) for a direct-mapped cache.
The directory does not include the data array. A question that asks for 'total cache size including tags' wants data + directory, which is a different sum.

example.prompt: GATE CSE 2011 Q.43: an 8 KB direct-mapped write-back cache with 32 B blocks, 32-bit addresses, one valid bit and one modified bit per line. Total metadata size?
example.work: Lines = 8192/32 = 256, so index 8; offset 5; tag = 32 - 8 - 5 = 19. Per entry 19 + 1 + 1 = 21 bits. Total = 256 x 21 = 5376 bits.

gateAngle: The trap is arithmetic, not concept: one forgotten bit per entry moves the answer by 256 bits, and the options are built around exactly that. Compute bits per entry first, multiply last.

variations.label: VERIFIED PYQ
variations.question: GATE CSE 2011 Q.43, as worked above.
variations.why: 19 tag bits plus valid and modified bits, times 256 lines. Dropping the two flag bits gives 4864 bits, which is option A.

variations.label: ORIGINAL PYQ-STYLE QUESTION
variations.question: A 64 KB 4-way cache has 32 B blocks, 40-bit addresses, and each entry carries a valid bit, a dirty bit and 2 replacement bits. What is the directory size?
variations.answer: 2048 lines, 512 sets, index 9; offset 5; tag = 40 - 9 - 5 = 26. Per entry 26 + 4 = 30 bits. Total = 2048 x 30 = 61440 bits = 60 Kbits.
variations.why: It adds replacement bits and a 40-bit address, which is where candidates lose a bit or mis-set the index.

variations.label: CONCEPTUAL PRACTICE QUESTION
variations.question: Why is the directory much smaller than the data array?
variations.answer: Because it stores one tag per line, not one tag per word: a 64 B line with a 19-bit tag needs 21 metadata bits for 512 data bits.
variations.why: It explains why tags are cheap in area but still matter in every width question.

trap.what: Multiplying by the number of sets instead of the number of lines.
trap.why: Each line has its own tag and flags, so the entry count is the line count; the number of sets only tells you how many comparators there are.
trap.counterexample: A 4-way cache with 512 lines and 128 sets: 512 entries of 21 bits is 10752 bits; using 128 gives 2688 bits, a quarter of the right answer.

check.question: A 32 KB 2-way cache with 64 B blocks and 24-bit addresses needs a valid bit and a dirty bit per entry. Directory size?
check.answer: 512 lines, 256 sets, index 8; offset 6; tag = 24 - 8 - 6 = 10; per entry 12 bits; total 6144 bits.
check.explanation: 512 x 12 = 6144 bits, which is 768 bytes - small next to the 32 KB of data, which is the point.
